children: , the obesity and diabetes drugmaker, faces a growing field of challengers chasing a weight loss market that could reach $100 billion in annual sales. Shares rose about 3.6% to $1,192.91 at 10.51am ET Time on Thursday morning, measured against Wednesday's $1,150.99 close.

Lilly has a head start challengers cannot buy overnight. Its second-quarter revenue surged 48% to $23 billion, powered chiefly by demand for Mounjaro and Zepbound. The company also has the approved Foundayo pill and retatrutide in late-stage development. That gives it several ways to compete as patients and doctors weigh injections against pills.

The picture puts Lilly's share price 23.27% below its roughly $1,550 GF Value estimate. That gap is striking, but it is no guarantee of upside. New treatments could squeeze prices or take share; Lilly's test is whether its manufacturing capacity and established medicines can keep sales growing as the field gets crowded.

title: Lilly Jumps 3.64% While a $100 Billion Obesity Race Crowds In
